probe.name: github_events_passive_server_witness_audit
probe.question: Can GitHub Events/PushEvent act as a zero-extra-mutation, server-generated timestamp and retention witness for an already-authorized cross_field repository-local checkpoint push, while satisfying independent-witness semantics?
probe.tested_scope: Official GitHub.com REST Events and GitHub event-type contracts, plus the already-authorized cross_field r297 checkpoint/commit identity. No O, downstream, other-worker state, private mailbox/calendar content, external-account mutation, scheduler mutation, hosted compute, paid API, or finite-credit service was used.

facts_used: Events are triggered by activity on GitHub.
The timeline includes at most 300 events and only events created within the past 30 days.
Repository/public event endpoints are list/read surfaces; public resources can be read without authentication.
Event API latency may range from about 30 seconds to 6 hours.
Every event has an id, actor, repo, public flag, payload and created_at timestamp.
PushEvent is triggered when one or more commits are pushed.
PushEvent payload includes repository_id, push_id, ref, head and before, binding the event to a pushed head commit SHA.

observations: GitHub's documented event object supplies a server-side created_at plus unique event id, actor and repository identity.
The documented PushEvent payload binds the event to the pushed ref and head/before commit SHAs.
The documented Events timeline is explicitly finite: at most 300 events and only the past 30 days.
The documented Events API family used for this candidate exposes listing/read behavior rather than an event-edit endpoint.

The connected GitHub connector in this invocation did not expose the repository-events collection: an attempted read of /repos/bachikoljunior-blip/note/events was rejected by the connector allowlist, so the concrete PushEvent for checkpoint commit ca34c6a230d40fdc699e4684846d3a5d9e9ace80 was not directly observed.
inferences: If the normal checkpoint push generated a PushEvent as the public contract specifies for pushes, it would provide a provider-generated timestamp and commit-head binding without any additional mutation, recipient, secret, user action, finite quota, or incremental monetary cost.
That record is not an independent witness of the GitHub commit because both the commit hosting and event record are controlled and retained by the same provider, GitHub.
The 30-day/300-event retention bound independently defeats a durable long-horizon witness requirement even if the event itself is not directly user-editable through the Events API.
Therefore GitHub Events is useful only as a short-lived same-provider liveness/timestamp corroborator, not as the independent-retention witness sought by this frontier.
unverified: The exact PushEvent id/created_at for checkpoint commit ca34c6a230d40fdc699e4684846d3a5d9e9ace80 was not observed in-run because the connected GitHub read surface rejected the repository-events endpoint.
No claim is made that GitHub guarantees archival retention beyond the documented Events timeline.

comparison.github_events: No extra mutation and strong commit-SHA binding, but same-provider control plus 30-day/300-event retention make it fail independent durable-witness semantics.
comparison.r297_gmail_calendar: A distinct provider can supply server timestamps, but the tested safe routes required an external send/attendee-style side effect or remained user-editable, so no authorized independent witness was established.
comparison.open_timestamps: Remains the stronger independence benchmark from r297 because its intended trust separation is external to GitHub; however this role still lacks an established scheduled-Chat mutation path to a free calendar server under the current write boundary.

phase1_constraints.residual_richer_mode_protected_or_manual: UNRESOLVED for an independently retained witness reachable only through currently authorized scheduled-Chat surfaces
phase1_constraints.conflict_or_duplication_risk: LOW for this read/contract audit; no shared or external mutation performed
phase1_constraints.scope_guard: Negative conclusion applies to GitHub Events/PushEvent as the independent durable-witness candidate under the documented 30-day/300-event timeline, not to all possible third-party archives of GitHub events.

frontier: GitHub Events supplies server-generated created_at and commit-head binding with no extra write, but fails independence and durable retention.

A passive third-party archive that automatically ingests public GitHub PushEvents could remove the extra-mutation problem while adding provider separation; it must still pass retention, identity-binding, replayability, zero-quota and zero-cost gates.

The most promising next bounded candidate is GH Archive (or a comparable public third-party GitHub-event archive) because it may independently retain public PushEvents without requiring the scheduled Chat agent to mutate an external account.
exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap current manifest/lifecycle/root/config and reconstruct r298 from LATEST. Execute exactly one bounded CLEAN child: audit GH Archive or the strongest comparable passive third-party public GitHub-event archive as an independent witness automatically ingesting public PushEvents. Test whether bachikoljunior-blip/note public checkpoint pushes are in scope without any additional mutation or registration; verify retention horizon, raw-record availability, commit-head/ref identity binding, provider independence, replayability, user/admin rewritability, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota dependency and zero incremental monetary cost. Compare against the r298 GitHub-Events same-provider failure, r297 Gmail/Calendar and OpenTimestamps; fail closed if ingestion is not automatic/public, retention is not durable enough, or access requires quota-bearing hosted query/compute.
